top_stories.title: OpenAI helps Hyatt advance AI among colleagues
top_stories.summary: Hyatt has partnered with OpenAI to deploy ChatGPT Enterprise across its workforce, marking a significant expansion of AI tools into the hospitality sector. The announcement details how Hyatt is using the platform to improve internal operations and colleague productivity. This is a primary source announcement from OpenAI's official blog.

top_stories.title: Tech CEOs Think AI Will Let Them Be Everywhere at Once
top_stories.summary: Wired reports on a growing trend of technology executives using AI tools to extend their presence and influence across organisations simultaneously. The piece examines how leaders are deploying AI to replicate their decision-making and communication at scale. It raises questions about the nature of leadership and accountability in an AI-augmented workplace.

top_stories.title: Deezer says 44% of songs uploaded to its platform daily are AI-generated
top_stories.summary: Music streaming platform Deezer has revealed that nearly half of all tracks uploaded to its platform each day are AI-generated, highlighting the rapid proliferation of synthetic content in the music industry. The figure underscores growing challenges for platforms managing content authenticity and creator rights. The story was reported by TechCrunch.

top_stories.title: Chinese tech workers are starting to train their AI doubles–and pushing back
top_stories.summary: MIT Technology Review reports on Chinese technology workers being asked to train AI systems modelled on their own work patterns and outputs — effectively creating AI versions of themselves. Some workers are resisting the practice, raising concerns about job displacement and exploitation of their professional knowledge. The piece highlights a new frontier of tension between AI adoption and labour rights.

top_stories.title: Atlassian enables default data collection to train AI
top_stories.summary: Atlassian has quietly changed its settings to enable data collection from users by default to train its AI systems, according to a report from Let's Data Science. The move has drawn attention from privacy advocates and enterprise customers who may be unaware their data is being used. The change reflects a broader industry pattern of software companies leveraging customer data for AI development.

further_links.title: Import AI 454: Automating alignment research; safety study of a Chinese model; HiFloat4
further_links.summary: Jack Clark's Import AI newsletter covers the latest in AI safety research, including efforts to automate alignment research and a safety evaluation of a prominent Chinese AI model.

further_links.title: Fortnite developers can make AI characters now — just don't try to date them
further_links.summary: Epic Games is enabling Fortnite developers to create AI-driven characters with conversational abilities, while setting content policy guardrails against romantic interactions.

further_links.title: The Download: murderous 'mirror' bacteria, and Chinese workers fighting AI doubles
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review's daily briefing covers the controversy over synthetic mirror bacteria research alongside the growing worker resistance to AI doubles in Chinese tech firms.

further_links.title: Silicon Valley has forgotten what normal people want
further_links.summary: The Verge argues that tech industry priorities — from NFTs to the metaverse to AI — have consistently diverged from what mainstream users actually find useful or desirable.

further_links.title: A Humanoid Robot Set a Half-Marathon Record in China
further_links.summary: A humanoid robot completed a half-marathon in China, setting a new record and demonstrating significant advances in bipedal locomotion and endurance for robotics systems.

further_links.title: Cloud development platform Vercel was hacked
further_links.summary: The Verge reports that Vercel, a widely used cloud development and deployment platform, suffered a security breach, raising concerns for developers and AI application builders who rely on its infrastructure.

further_links.title: Musk claims Grok 5.0 will achieve AGI, but is he right?
further_links.summary: Elon Musk has claimed that xAI's forthcoming Grok 5.0 model will reach artificial general intelligence, prompting scrutiny from researchers and commentators over what AGI means and whether such a claim is credible.
